lines.trans: Dear Robson, cut the green and yellow one, okay?
The red one is inactive, Robson. The signal is at zero.
Look at that, the red one is inactive, it does nothing.
The green and yellow one is working at full load.
Bringing wealth to us, working, bringing good things.
While the red one is slacking off, doing nothing.
And this is the guy I cannot cut?
If you touch those pliers to the red one, the whole block will get blown away.
Hold on, boss. It is very easy to fall for the detonator's narrative, right?

meanings.note: Warm Brazilian vocative used even with strangers.

examples.trans: Excuse me, my friend.
I do not have change, pal.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Você precisa cortar o fio verde.
examples.trans: You need to cut the green wire.
Cut that wire right now!

meanings.note: Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: What is your job title?
Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Color of grass and the main field of Brazil's flag.

examples.text: Corta o fio verde e amarelo.
examples.trans: Cut the green and yellow wire.
The light is already green.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction pronounced [i] in natural Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Ela faltou e adiantou o trabalho.
examples.trans: She missed it and got ahead on her work.
There are good and bad numbers.

meanings.note: Color of gold or ripe lemons; paired with verde for Brazil's flag colors.

examples.text: Você precisa cortar o fio verde e amarelo.
examples.trans: You need to cut the green and yellow wire.
She bought a yellow shirt.

meanings.note: Conversational final tag seeking agreement or emphasis.

examples.trans: Cut that wire right now, okay?
Wow, that is wild, huh?

meanings.note: Color of rubies or danger wires; also associated with left-wing politics.

examples.trans: This red wire is inactive.
Our wiring will never be red!

meanings.note: Used here for being present at an event. Vou estar keeps estar in the infinitive after the finite form vou.

examples.trans: I’m not going to be at that meeting.
Are you going to be at that meeting?

meanings.note: Not carrying a signal or not operating.

examples.trans: The red wire is inactive.

examples.text: A conta ficou inativa por meses.
examples.trans: The account was inactive for months.

meanings.note: Electrical or communication signal.

examples.trans: The signal is completely at zero.
I have no signal on my phone.

meanings.note: Showing a reading of zero.

examples.trans: The signal is completely at zero.
The meter went down to zero.

meanings.note: Used as a quick imperative olha! (look!) and in future subjunctive se vocês olharem (if you look).

examples.trans: Look inside there.

examples.text: Se vocês olharem bem, tem números.
examples.trans: If you look closely, there are numbers.

meanings.note: Adds immediacy after imperatives like calma aí, or means there near you.

examples.trans: Hang on!
Who is there?

meanings.note: A negative answer or a negation in a sentence. A final repeated não can reinforce a conversational refusal in Brazil.

examples.trans: No, I’m not going.
Aren’t you going?

meanings.note: Irregular past eu fiz (I made/did); não tem o que fazer means having nothing to do.

examples.text: Ela não tem o que fazer agora.
examples.trans: She has nothing to do now.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

meanings.note: Used with nem or não for emphatic negation.

examples.text: Você nem comentou nada do implante?
examples.trans: You did not even mention anything about the implant?
I have nothing to say.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Sim, eu trabalho aqui no restaurante.
examples.trans: Yes, I work here at the restaurant.

examples.text: O fio está trabalhando com carga total.
examples.trans: The wire is working at full load.

meanings.note: Marks accompaniment or an added ingredient such as sweetener.

examples.trans: I want coffee with sweetener.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.
examples.trans: She is with our team.

meanings.note: Electrical charge or workload; com carga total means at full capacity.

examples.text: O fio está trabalhando com carga total.
examples.trans: The wire is working at full load.
The battery has no charge.

meanings.note: Complete or maximum.

examples.trans: It is working at full load.
We have the team's full support.

meanings.note: Irregular past trouxe and gerund trazendo.

examples.text: Olha o que eu trouxe para nós.
examples.trans: Look what I brought for us.

examples.text: Esse trabalho está trazendo coisa boa.
examples.trans: This work is bringing good things.

meanings.note: Abundance of valuable resources or money.

examples.trans: This sector is bringing wealth.
Work produces wealth.

meanings.note: Informal reduced para. Before a feminine noun, this Brazilian spelling can also represent a contraction including the article a; the exact meeting is clear from context.

examples.trans: I’m going to the meeting.
Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Alone as vocative gente! it means folks/guys; with article a gente it means we/us with third-person singular verbs.

examples.text: Você acha que é melhor que a gente?
examples.trans: Do you think you're better than us?
Oh, folks, the meeting ran late.

meanings.note: Very frequent general noun; singular muita coisa naturally translates as a lot of things.

examples.trans: I have a lot to sort out.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.
examples.trans: Let me tell you something.

meanings.note: Everyday adjective in tá bom (okay), boa tarde (good afternoon), and Bom, pessoal (Well, folks).

examples.trans: All right, I'll go.
Some numbers are good.

meanings.note: Contrasts two simultaneous actions or situations.

examples.text: Um trabalha enquanto o outro descansa.
examples.trans: One works while the other rests.
Wait here while I come back.

meanings.note: Colloquially means living off others or doing no work.

examples.text: O fio vermelho está encostado, sem fazer nada.
examples.trans: The red wire is slacking off, doing nothing.

examples.text: O carro ficou encostado na oficina.
examples.trans: The car sat idle in the repair shop.

meanings.note: Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.

examples.trans: I’m in finance.
It’s a marketing meeting.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner; in spoken Brazilian Portuguese esse commonly covers both this near me and that just mentioned.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

examples.text: Vou ficar sentado esse tempo inteiro.
examples.trans: I'm going to stay seated that whole time.

meanings.note: Informal masculine noun meaning guy, dude, or man; as a feminine noun it literally means face.

examples.trans: What is this, man?
The guy canceled the meeting.

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.
What is this, man?

meanings.note: Subject form referring to the speaker. Explicit eu introduces his department in the explanation.

examples.trans: I’m in finance.
I’m not going.

poder.gloss: can; may; to be able to

meanings.en: can; may; to be able to
meanings.note: Core modal verb followed by an infinitive.

examples.text: O senhor pode ser meu fiador?
examples.trans: Can you be my guarantor, sir?
I cannot right now.

meanings.note: Introduces a condition; triggers future subjunctive when referring to a possible future action (se vocês olharem).

examples.text: Se eu vou entrar, você vai também.
examples.trans: If I'm going in, you're going too.

examples.text: Se vocês olharem bem, tem números.
examples.trans: If you look closely, there are numbers.

meanings.note: A person being addressed, with third-person verb agreement: você vai, vocês vão. Vai and vão are forms of ir, not forms of the pronoun. Common in Brazil; not a rule that every Brazilian region uses the same address system.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?
Are you in finance?

meanings.note: Encostar X em Y means to touch X against Y.

examples.text: Não encoste esse alicate no fio.
examples.trans: Do not touch those pliers to the wire.

examples.text: Ele encostou a bicicleta no muro.
examples.trans: He leaned the bicycle against the wall.

meanings.note: Hand tool used for gripping or cutting wires.

examples.text: Não encoste esse alicate no fio.
examples.trans: Do not touch those pliers to the wire.
I need a new pair of pliers.

meanings.note: Usually contracts with definite articles to no, na, nos, nas.

examples.trans: He is in the meeting.
She stays on her phone.

meanings.note: Urban block surrounded by streets.

examples.text: O quarteirão inteiro vai pro espaço.
examples.trans: The whole city block will get blown away.
I walked around the block.

meanings.note: Placed after the noun (esse tempo inteiro) to emphasize completeness.

examples.trans: I stayed there that whole time.
I worked the entire morning.

meanings.note: Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.

examples.trans: I’m going to the meeting.
Aren’t you going?

meanings.note: In ir pro espaço, colloquial idiom meaning to get blown up or ruined.

examples.text: O quarteirão inteiro vai pro espaço.
examples.trans: The whole block will get blown away.
There is not enough space in this room.

meanings.note: Used standalone or as calma aí! to tell someone to slow down and relax.

examples.trans: Easy, that's not it!
Hang on, I'm coming.

meanings.note: Informal form of address to a supervisor or team leader.

examples.trans: Hold on, boss.

examples.text: O chefe pediu o relatório hoje.
examples.trans: The boss asked for the report today.

meanings.note: Agrees with its noun as a determiner/adjective; singular muita coisa idiomatically means many things.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.
I have many numbers here.

meanings.note: Plural fáceis.

examples.text: Fica mais fácil pra abrir e fechar.
examples.trans: It gets easier to open and close.
That is easy to understand.

meanings.note: Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.

examples.trans: It’s a marketing meeting.
I’m in finance.

meanings.note: Used for objects dropping or buttons coming loose.

examples.text: Se cair um botão, você tira outro.
examples.trans: If a button falls off, you take another.
The phone fell on the floor.

meanings.note: Story or ideological framing of events.

examples.text: É fácil cair na narrativa deles.
examples.trans: It is easy to fall for their narrative.

examples.text: Cada lado conta uma narrativa diferente.
examples.trans: Each side tells a different narrative.

meanings.note: Device that triggers an explosive charge.

examples.text: O vermelho está ligado no detonador.
examples.trans: The red one is connected to the detonator.
The detonator draws power directly.

meanings.note: Ubiquitous spoken contraction of não é used to invite agreement.

examples.text: Isso aqui é um gráfico, né?
examples.trans: This here is a chart, right?
It's Monday, right?

meanings.note: Written as one word without an accent in answers and explanations.

examples.text: Estou aqui porque venderam o apartamento.
examples.trans: I am here because they sold the apartment.

examples.text: Porque ninguém tem fé na gente.
examples.trans: Because nobody has faith in us.

meanings.note: The science of matter, energy, and forces.

examples.trans: Just because physics says so.
He teaches physics.

meanings.note: Irregular 3rd singular present diz.

examples.trans: Just because physics says so.
What does the report say?

meanings.note: Technical diagram or mapping of a system.

examples.trans: I do not trust electronic mapping.
I want the printed mapping.

meanings.note: Operating by digital or electronic means.

examples.trans: I do not trust electronic mapping.
I received the electronic document.

meanings.note: In até logo it looks ahead to the next meeting. The phrase is added as the lesson farewell, not quoted from the selected source window.

examples.trans: See you later!
See you later. Thanks!

meanings.note: Marks comparisons (mais que), negated continuation (não ... mais, not anymore), and the farewell até mais.

examples.trans: He isn't coming anymore.
See you later!
